newsitem.title: USA: Agreement reached to reopen Chicago airport.
newsitem.headline: Agreement reached to reopen Chicago airport.

text.p: A small airport on Chicago's downtown lakefront will reopen for a limited time before being bulldozed for a $27 million, bond-financed nature park under an agreement announced Monday by Chicago Mayor Richard Daley.

Speaking at a news conference at city hall, Daley said Meigs Field would be reopened "very soon" for a five-year period, after which time the city and Chicago Park District would implement their plan to turn the airport into a park.
The agreement with Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar also dismisses lawsuits the state had filed to block the park plans, Daley said.
He added that he and Edgar would work to repeal legislation passed by the Illinois General Assembly late last year allowing the state to takeover the airport.

The deal came just as Republican lawmakers in Springfield were poised to approve another airport takeover bill that would have immediate effect. The one passed last year and signed into law Dec. 16 by Edgar lacked a three-fifths majority vote for immediate effect postponing its effective date to June 1.
The agreement also followed a proposal by Edgar to keep the airport, used mainly by business and state aircraft, open for seven years.
